messages.subject: Integrating multiple Imputations from "mice" to "mirt"
parts:
Hi Phil,

I currently have a dataset with around 10% missing values.
I used the imputations available in the mirt package, but I also wanted to use MI from the mice package and compare results. I have already imputed the data but I am struggeling to find a way to calculate seperate Rasch-Models for all my imputation dataframe versions.

Imagine df_imputed is an object created by the mice function with 20 multiple imputations. How would the code in mirt look like, if I wanted to calculate a Rasch-Model for all versions? And how would I pool the results?

Thank you very very much!

Nick

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Integrating multiple Imputations from "mice" to "mirt"
parts:
Hi Nick,

I would generally advise against using mirt's MI methods for missing data (they are model-based and inherently conservative), so MI would be the way to go. In terms of the code you would likely run the 20 models, store them as a list, and pool the results using Rubin's method. I have added some support for this via the function averageMI() (https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/docs/reference/averageMI.html). Does that help?

Phil
